_what: Which files hold NUMBERS MEASURED from the world, which hold the model's OPINIONS about the world, and which are about this machine. The first two are split on purpose: telling them apart is the point of the project.
_who: Human-written. tools/attention_ratio.py reads it and never guesses beyond it.
_drafted: 2026-08-28. Six files were opened and classified the same evening; one remains open.
_rule: A file nobody has opened is LEFT OUT, so it shows up as UNCLASSIFIED and a human decides. An unclassified pile is the tool refusing to decide what it should not decide.

_classified_2026-08-28.memory/grounding_ledger.jsonl: MEASURED. 53 rows, each carrying real anchor and daily values with org and age_days (NOAA-GML 424.98 vs anchor 428.72), hash-chained. It is the seam, but its content is world numbers with provenance.
_classified_2026-08-28.memory/llm_provenance.jsonl: SELF. 3565 rows of backend, model, caller, prompt_sha, tokens, finish_reason. A record of the machine's own calls. Nothing in a row is about the world.
_classified_2026-08-28.memory/knowledge_base.json: ASSERTED. 28 axes, each with cycle_count and key_insights - the model's prose about problems and root causes. About the world, never from it.
_classified_2026-08-28.memory/problem_solution_db.json: SELF. 26 keys of attempted_solutions with dates, actions and results including Python tracebacks. The machine's own repair attempts.
_classified_2026-08-28.memory/source_lifecycle_ledger.jsonl: MEASURED. clean/refusal outcomes of real fetches, with values and states. It measures how the world's data providers actually behaved.

_deliberately_unclassified.memory/intel.db: 12 MB sqlite, media intelligence. NOT OPENED. World if it stores transcripts of real events, self if it stores the machine's reading habits. Open it before placing it - do not guess from the name.

_corrected_2026-08-29: snapshots/**/*.json claimed the whole snapshots tree for the world. 99.2% of what it matched - 13.58 MB of 13.68 MB - was snapshots/self/, this machine's snapshots of itself. Correcting only that glob moves self-per-measured from 0.69 to 2.39 and reverses the tool's central claim. Found by running it, not by reading it. The map was wrong; the tool did exactly what it was told, which is why the tool now REFUSES to place a file two sides both claim.
